paragraphs.text: On a hot summer afternoon, the centre of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the countryside around it. This effect, known as the urban heat island, was first described in the early nineteenth century by Luke Howard, an amateur scientist who recorded temperatures in and around London over many years. He noticed that the difference was greatest not in the afternoon but at night.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The reasons are now well understood. Dark roads and roofs absorb sunlight during the day and release the stored heat slowly after sunset. Tall buildings trap this warm air and block the wind that might otherwise carry it away. Cars, air-conditioning units and factories add further heat, and because cities have fewer trees and less open soil, there is less water evaporating to cool the air.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Higher temperatures are not simply uncomfortable. During heatwaves, the number of deaths in cities rises sharply, particularly among elderly people living alone. Warm nights are especially dangerous, because the body has no chance to recover from the heat of the day. Demand for electricity also increases as more people switch on air-conditioning, which in turn releases more heat into the streets.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Cities have tried a range of responses. Some paint roofs white or cover them with light-coloured materials that reflect sunlight. Others plant trees along streets, since a single mature tree can cool the air around it through shade and evaporation. In one European city, replacing a car park with a small park lowered the temperature of the surrounding streets by around two degrees on summer evenings.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: None of these measures is a complete solution. White roofs reduce the need for cooling in summer but can increase heating costs in winter in colder climates. Trees take many years to grow and need water, which may be scarce during the very heatwaves they are meant to relieve. Many planners now argue that the best results come from combining several small changes rather than relying on a single large project.
paragraphs.label: E

items.prompt: Luke Howard was a professional scientist.

explanation.en: “an amateur scientist” — an amateur, not a professional → FALSE.
explanation.kk: «an amateur scientist» — кәсіпқой емес, әуесқой ғалым → FALSE.
explanation.ru: «an amateur scientist» — любитель, а не профессионал → FALSE.

items.quote: the difference was greatest not in the afternoon but at night
items.prompt: Howard found that the temperature difference was largest at night.

explanation.en: “He noticed that the difference was greatest not in the afternoon but at night”. “Largest” is a synonym of “greatest” → TRUE.
explanation.kk: «He noticed that the difference was greatest not in the afternoon but at night» — Ховард айырмашылық түнде ең үлкен болатынын байқаған. «Largest» — «greatest» сөзінің синонимі → TRUE.
explanation.ru: «He noticed that the difference was greatest not in the afternoon but at night» — Ховард заметил, что разница больше всего ночью. «Largest» — синоним «greatest» → TRUE.

items.quote: recorded temperatures in and around London over many years
items.prompt: Howard’s measurements were used to plan new buildings in London.

explanation.en: The text says Howard recorded temperatures in London. How his data was used is not mentioned → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Ховард Лондонда температураны жазып отырғаны айтылған. Оның деректері қалай пайдаланылғаны мәтінде жоқ → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Сказано, что Ховард записывал температуру в Лондоне. Как использовались его данные, текст не сообщает → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: release the stored heat slowly after sunset
items.prompt: Dark surfaces lose their stored heat quickly after sunset.

explanation.en: “release the stored heat slowly after sunset” — slowly, but the statement says “quickly” → FALSE.
explanation.kk: «release the stored heat slowly after sunset» — баяу, ал тұжырымда «quickly» делінген → FALSE.
explanation.ru: «release the stored heat slowly after sunset» — медленно, а в утверждении «quickly» → FALSE.

items.quote: because cities have fewer trees and less open soil, there is less water evaporating to cool the air
items.prompt: Trees and soil help to cool the air through evaporation.

explanation.en: Fewer trees and less soil → “less water evaporating to cool the air”. So trees and soil cool the air through evaporation → TRUE. You need to follow the “less A → less B” logic.
explanation.kk: Ағаш пен топырақ аз → «less water evaporating to cool the air». Демек ағаш пен топырақ ауаны буландыру арқылы салқындатады → TRUE. «А аз болса, Б да аз» деген логиканы түсіну керек.
explanation.ru: Меньше деревьев и почвы → «less water evaporating to cool the air». Значит, деревья и почва охлаждают воздух за счёт испарения → TRUE. Здесь нужно понять логику «меньше А → меньше Б».

items.quote: the number of deaths in cities rises sharply, particularly among elderly people living alone
items.prompt: Heatwaves are particularly dangerous for elderly people who live alone.

explanation.en: “deaths … rises sharply, particularly among elderly people living alone” — deaths rise most in this group = “particularly dangerous” → TRUE.
explanation.kk: «deaths … rises sharply, particularly among elderly people living alone» — өлім дәл осы топта көбейеді = «particularly dangerous» → TRUE.
explanation.ru: «deaths … rises sharply, particularly among elderly people living alone» — рост смертности именно в этой группе = «particularly dangerous» → TRUE.

items.quote: which in turn releases more heat into the streets
items.prompt: Using air-conditioning makes city streets cooler.

explanation.en: Air-conditioning cools rooms, but it “releases more heat into the streets” — streets get warmer → FALSE.
explanation.kk: Кондиционер бөлмені салқындатады, бірақ «releases more heat into the streets» — көшеде жылырақ болады → FALSE.
explanation.ru: Кондиционер охлаждает помещение, но «releases more heat into the streets» — на улице становится теплее → FALSE.

items.quote: Some paint roofs white or cover them with light-coloured materials that reflect sunlight
items.prompt: White roofs are cheaper to install than planting street trees.

explanation.en: Both measures are named, but their costs are never compared. Paragraph E mentions heating costs, not installation prices → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Екі тәсіл де аталған, бірақ олардың бағасы мәтінде салыстырылмайды. E абзацы жылыту шығыны туралы, орнату бағасы туралы емес → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Оба способа названы, но их стоимость не сравнивается нигде в тексте. Абзац E говорит о расходах на отопление, а не о цене установки → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: replacing a car park with a small park lowered the temperature of the surrounding streets
items.prompt: The car park was replaced mainly in order to reduce traffic.

explanation.en: The text gives the result (the streets were two degrees cooler) but not the reason for the change. Traffic is not mentioned → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Мәтін нәтижені айтады (көшелер екі градусқа салқындаған), бірақ автотұрақты не үшін ауыстырғанын айтпайды. Көлік қозғалысы туралы сөз жоқ → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Текст сообщает результат (улицы остыли на два градуса), но причину замены парковки не называет. Про транспорт — ни слова → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: the best results come from combining several small changes rather than relying on a single large project
items.prompt: Planners generally prefer one large project to several small changes.

explanation.en: “combining several small changes rather than relying on a single large project” — planners favour small changes, not one large project → FALSE.
explanation.kk: «combining several small changes rather than relying on a single large project» — жоспарлаушылар бір ірі жобаны емес, бірнеше шағын өзгерісті қолдайды → FALSE.
explanation.ru: «combining several small changes rather than relying on a single large project» — планировщики за несколько небольших мер, а не за один проект → FALSE.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–10. Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, or NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.
